From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Evidence phasing & audit gate alignment — ISO/FedRAMP quick sync

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. We want to lock a short cadence to align how we phase evidence for ISO 27001 and FedRAMP so your audit window has minimal disruption to your infra team. High level ask: can you confirm which of the following intake/gating expectations work for Acme Financial?

1) Evidence phasing (we propose):
   - Phase 1 (initial intake, 2 weeks): control narratives, key policy docs, and network/topology diagram
   - Phase 2 (sampling, 3 weeks): log snapshots, IAM role lists, config screenshots, and sample user access records
   - Phase 3 (final handback, 1 week): compiled control matrix and auditor-ready bundles

2) SIG/CAIQ gating: we plan to accept CAIQ exports first and then request SIG clarifications for any non-automatable controls. Will that sequencing work?

3) Owners & SLAs: suggest owners from our side below — please assign counterpart owners on your side so we can start intake automation.

Attached: proposed phasing workbook (redwood-evidence-phasing.xlsx) and a sample intake CSV (fedramp-intake-template.csv).

Action items I’m proposing:
- Acme: confirm owners and any blackout dates by EOD Tue (4/27)
- Redwood: populate control-mapping draft and sample list (we’ll circulate)

If that sounds good I’ll put a 30-min sync on Wed to finalize.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

High level ask: can you confirm which of the following intake/gating expectations work for Acme Financial?

Thanks, Evelyn — I like the phased approach. A couple of notes from the intake/process side:

- For Phase 2 (sampling), please confirm whether you need raw syslog exports or compressed daily snapshots (we can accept either, but sampling rules differ).
- We typically request a 3-business-day SLA on initial evidence delivery for items flagged as 'high priority' in the CAIQ. That keeps the auditor dry-run on schedule.
- I attached a short control mapping (control-mapping-v2.pdf) that maps Redwood controls to CAIQ sections; it helps speed the SIG follow-up.

Proposed owners (Redwood):
- Intake lead: Kimberly Park (kimberly.park@redwood.com) — automation & sample extraction
- Control narratives: Markus Klein (markus.klein@redwood.com) — narratives and control crosswalk
- Audit liaison: Aditya Rao (aditya.rao@redwood.com) — scheduling and escalation

If Acme can confirm their owners and the log format preference by Tue we can seed the intake automation and generate pre-signed S3 links for secure uploads.

Kimberly
Director, Compliance Automation
Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Kimberly — thanks for the clear plan. Quick responses from Acme side:

- Owners: I will own the intake from Acme (Aisha Roy, aisha.roy@acmecorp.com). Tom Nguyen will coordinate on infra uploads.
- Log format: we can provide compressed daily snapshots (gz) for the last 90 days; will that satisfy sampling?
- Blackout dates: we have a maintenance window the week of 5/10 — please avoid heavy requests then.

One ask: can Redwood provide an example of the 'auditor-ready bundle' structure? Our procurement/audit team needs to see the expected folder layout and redaction guidance before we start extracting records. If you have a short doc (or a sample zipped bundle) please share.

Also note procurement prefers DocuSign for any data access addendums. I can route to our legal once we have the intake S3 URL and the Docusign link.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Roy

Acme Financial
